disclaimer: Computed from published screening methodologies (AAOIFI SS 21, FTSE Yasaar, MSCI Islamic) — we are not a Sharia board and this is not a fatwa, not financial advice, and not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Every figure is date-stamped and decays; missing data is shown as 'insufficient data', never guessed. Verify against primary sources and consult a qualified scholar before acting.
methodology_note: Overall verdict basis: AAOIFI SS 21. FTSE Yasaar and MSCI Islamic results are shown side by side because the standards genuinely disagree (denominators, thresholds, sector exclusions) — the same company can pass one and fail another. Expand any test to see the worked math.
conventions: AAOIFI ratios use SPOT market capitalization per SS 21 clause 3/4/5 ('last verified financial position'); trailing averages are screener conventions, not standard text.
TradingView total_debt_fq proxies interest-bearing debt; whether it includes operating-lease liabilities is a known screener divergence point (cross-validated in tests, disclosed here).
Total cash + short-term investments proxies interest-bearing deposits and securities (conservative: overstates the numerator).
Receivables are approximated as revenue_fy / receivables_turnover_fy (average AR); exact point-in-time AR arrives with SEC XBRL in v1.1.

business.note: Business-activity clean (permissible midstream). evidence.quote: FY2025 10-K (fiscal year ended Oct 31, 2025): Consolidated Statements of Earnings show Net Revenue of Products $21,956M, Services $11,573M, and Financing income $767M, for Total net revenue of $34,296M. Segment results: Financial Services total segment net revenue $3,504M (10.2% of consolidated), earnings from operations $361M; 'Financial Services net revenue decreased $8 million, or 0.2%, primarily due to lower rental revenue on lower average operating leases.' Lessor note: 'Interest income from sales-type leases and direct financing leases — Financing income — $767 [million]; Lease income from operating leases — Services — $2,156 [million]; Total lease income $2,923 [million].' FS portfolio: financing receivables gross $9,740M, net equipment under operating leases $3,159M, net portfolio assets $13,181M, debt-to-equity 7.0x, funded partly via asset-backed securitization (consolidated SPE/VIE).

impermissible_revenue_pct.basis: Strict interest-line basis: FY2025 'Financing income' (interest from sales-type and direct financing leases) $767M / consolidated net revenue $34,296M = 2.24%. Conservative whole-segment basis: entire captive Financial Services segment $3,504M / $34,296M = 10.2%. The gap is the decisive mix, now resolved from the lessor note: of FS-related revenue, $2,156M is operating-lease rental income (ijarah-like equipment leasing, generally permissible if the leased asset is halal — here IT equipment) and ~$581M is asset-management/remarketing/other services; only $767M is explicit interest income.

aaoifi.reason: Explicit interest revenue (Financing income $767M) is 2.24% of total revenue, below the 5% impermissible-income threshold. Operating-lease rentals ($2.16B, booked in Services) are structurally ijarah-like and most standards do not count them as impermissible. Business-activity screen passes on this basis; note this does not assess AAOIFI financial ratios (debt/market-cap etc.), which are out of scope for this file.

conservative_whole_segment.reason: If the entire captive-financing segment is treated as an impermissible conventional-finance business — defensible because FS originates conventional interest-bearing sales-type/direct-financing leases, runs a $13.2B portfolio at 7.0x debt-to-equity, and funds itself with interest-bearing asset-backed securitization — the segment is 10.2% of revenue, well above 5%. HPE itself lists IBM Global Financing, Dell Financial Services, Cisco Capital, banks and other financial institutions as FS's competitors, i.e., it is a finance business.

sector_exclusion.reason: Core business (servers ~52%, networking ~20%, hybrid cloud ~17% of revenue) is permissible IT hardware/software/services; no haram core sector. The issue is confined to the captive-financing arm.

screener_divergence.note: Interest-income-based screeners (Zoya/Musaffa-style, counting the $767M Financing income line) would likely pass HPE at ~2.2%; segment-based conservative screens fail it at ~10.2%. Hence 'questionable' rather than clean or prohibited. Watch item: effective Q1 FY2026 HPE merged Server, Hybrid Cloud, and Financial Services into one 'Cloud & AI' segment, so the FS revenue split will no longer be separately reported — future screening must rely on the Financing income line and the lessor note.

The decisive unknown (rental vs interest mix) is resolved: 61.5% of FS-related lease revenue is operating-lease rental ($2,156M), only $767M (2.24% of total revenue) is explicit financing interest. evidence.quote: 10-K Credit Karma segment note (FY ended 2025-07-31): "Total segment revenue $ 2,263 [million] ... % of total revenue 12 % ... Revenue for our Credit Karma segment increased $555 million, or 32%, in fiscal 2025 compared with fiscal 2024 due to increases in revenue from our personal loan vertical of $221 million, our credit card vertical of $213 million, and our auto insurance vertical of $99 million." Segment table: Credit Karma 2,263 of Total net revenue $18,831 million.

impermissible_revenue_pct.basis: segment-data

aaoifi.reason: Impermissible-activity revenue ~12.0% of total revenue ($2,263M Credit Karma / $18,831M total, FY2025) exceeds the 5% AAOIFI business-activity threshold. The Credit Karma segment monetizes cost-per-action referrals to interest-based credit products — the 10-K attributes FY2025 growth to the personal-loan vertical (+$221M), credit-card vertical (+$213M), and auto-insurance vertical (+$99M), i.e., riba-based lending referrals plus conventional insurance leads.

sector_exclusion.reason: Core business (TurboTax, QuickBooks, Mailchimp — tax/accounting/marketing software) is permissible; INTU fails on the revenue-share test, not on sector.

methodology_notes.scope_caveat: The 12% treats the entire Credit Karma segment as impermissible. A small slice (e.g., Credit Karma Money deposit accounts) is arguable, but the dominant verticals are loan/card/insurance referrals, so even a conservative sub-split stays well above 5%. Additional interest-linked revenue elsewhere (TurboTax Refund Advance, QuickBooks lending/payments float) is NOT counted here; including it would only raise the figure. Note: effective 2025-08-01 Intuit merged Credit Karma into a combined Consumer segment for FY2026 reporting, so this segment-level visibility degrades next fiscal year.

business.note: Evidence supports the target status. Cross-checked against the Intuit IR press release of 2025-08-21 (https://investors.intuit.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1266/...): "Grew Credit Karma revenue 32 percent to $2.3 billion" and Q4 growth "driven by strength in personal loans, credit cards, and auto insurance" — consistent with the 10-K exact figure of $2,263M. The press release only rounds to $2.3B; the exact $2,263M and the +$221M/+$213M/+$99M vertical breakdown come from the FY2025 10-K MD&A (filed 2025-09-03), which is the cited primary source.
